title: Possible Bipartition
prompt:
We want to split a group of `n` people (labeled `1` to `n`) into two groups of any size. Each person may dislike some other people, and they should not go into the same group.

Given `n` and the array `dislikes` where `dislikes[i] = [ai, bi]` indicates that person `ai` and person `bi` dislike each other, return `true` if it is possible to split everyone into two groups satisfying this condition, or `false` otherwise.

examples.explanation: Group 1: {1,4}, group 2: {2,3} — no two people in the same group dislike each other.
Persons 1, 2, and 3 mutually dislike each other, forming a triangle — impossible to 2-color.

constraints: All the pairs of dislikes are unique
hints: This is the same underlying question as graph bipartiteness: can you 2-color the people so no disliking pair shares a color?
Build an undirected graph where an edge means 'these two dislike each other,' then try to 2-color it via BFS or DFS, alternating colors as you traverse.

If you ever need to assign a color to a person who's already colored the opposite way required, a valid split is impossible. Check every connected component, since some people may have no listed dislikes at all.

solution.approach: Model dislikes as an undirected graph and attempt a 2-coloring (equivalent to a bipartite check): BFS from each uncolored person, assigning the opposite color to every disliked neighbor. If a neighbor is already colored the same as the current person, that pair is forced into the same group despite disliking each other, so a valid split is impossible. Successfully 2-coloring every component means the two groups are exactly the two color classes.
